questions.a: Fabrics are made of yarns, and yarns are made of thin strands called fibres.

questions.q: How can you show that fabric is made of yarns?
questions.a: Pull a thread from a piece of cloth and untwist it - it separates into fibres.

questions.q: Name two natural and two synthetic fabrics.
questions.a: Natural: cotton, silk, wool. Synthetic: nylon, polyester.

questions.q: Name two natural and two synthetic fibres.
questions.a: Natural: cotton and wool (also silk, jute). Synthetic: nylon and polyester.

questions.q: From which plant does cotton fibre come?
questions.a: From the cotton boll - the fruity ball of the cotton plant.

questions.q: From which animal does wool come?
questions.a: Sheep (also goat, yak) - wool is their hair fleece.

solution_steps.name: yarn_length
solution_steps.explain: each fibre contributes its own length to the twisted yarn

questions.q: If 20 fibres, each contributing 50 cm, are twisted into one yarn, find the yarn length in cm and m.
A spinner twists 35 cotton fibres of 40 cm each. How long is the yarn in metres?
25 fibres of 60 cm are spun together. Calculate the yarn length.
If 18 fibres of 25 cm each make a yarn, what is its length in m?
A silk yarn uses 12 fibres of 75 cm each. Find its total length in metres.

solution_steps.name: fabric_area
solution_steps.explain: area of cloth = length times width

solution_steps.name: area_in_cm2
